newsitem.title: UK: UK medical group in Malaysian medical venture.
newsitem.headline: UK medical group in Malaysian medical venture.

text.p: UK medical group XperTech Ltd has joined forces with the Malaysian healthcare group Kumpulan Perubatan Sdn Bhd (KPJSB), part of the Johor Corp, in a 14 million Malaysian ringgit joint venture to manufacture medical equipment.

The two companies, both unlisted, said at a signing ceremony at the Malaysian embassy in London the two main products will be surgical devices to close wounds (known as sutures) and minimal invasive surgery equipment (MSI) as used in endoscopic surgery.
Production kicks off in July 1997, with the aim of floating the venture after five years.
Most of the output will be for export, targeting the East Asian, European and U.S. markets. The MIS equipment will mainly be for sales in the Far East.
The companies behind the venture said the Far East region offered huge opportunities, with its countries pumping spending into healthcare.
The sutures products will be aimed at the U.S. market in particular, with the group currently identifying niche areas such as dental surgery where there is scope for more sales.
Total sales for the venture are seen at $20 million in five years, said Margaret Robinson, managing director of XperTech.

The two partners are seen pumping a further five million ringgits into the venture in years to come. The sutures world market is estimated to be $1.4 billion, growing at 10-15 percent per annum. The minimum invasive surgery product market is seen at more than $1 billion.

Other products currently under development include building a health screening system into doorframes within doctors' surgeries and hospital buildings to scan patients going through and transmit data about their health to medical records.
This innovation is five to ten years down the line.
